title: New-model gateway rules and compatibility slate
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Purpose: define a concise, machine-checkable gateway contract for new open-model intake that captures runtime compatibility signals, pinning guidance, and automated acceptance gates. This ticket clarifies required metadata fields, runtime compatibility labels, acceptance tests and rollout steps so that model owners and runtime engineers can reliably onboard new open weights with predictable behavior on Redwood hosting, Dedicated and Private deployments.
background: We frequently accept community-submitted model weights that vary in tokenizer, KV cache layout, quantization compatibility and custom ops. Previous intake PRDs were fragmented and led to runtime surprises (tokenization mismatches, increased latency after a swap-in, and silent failures on on-prem GPU kernels). This slate establishes structured rules for the "model gateway" (the intake pipeline + automated sanity checks) and a clear pin/fallback policy for catalog entries.
goals: 1) Require a minimal compatibility declaration that allows automated runtime mapping. 2) Prevent silent regressions by enforcing sanity tests and canary rollouts. 3) Define pinning semantics and automatic fallback behavior. 4) Reduce manual triage by surfacing deterministic incompatibility reasons in the intake UI.
out_of_scope: Deep research into new kernel implementations, full provenance verification of weights, commercial legal review of community licenses (handled by Legal).
requirements: A) Intake form fields: tokenizer_family, expected_vocab_hash, kv_layout_signature, supported_sequence_max, preferred_precision (fp16/int8/q4), op_extensions list, canonical_dockerfile reference. B) Compatibility labels that must be set: runtime-compatible | soft-pin | hard-incompatible | requires-adapter. C) Automated sanity tests: tokenization roundtrip (50 prompts), KV cache continuity test (resume generation across prefixes), cold-start latency bench (95th <= baseline*1.10), function-call schema test, deterministic output snapshot (approx similarity threshold). D) Pin/rollback behavior: new unpinned variants go to canary pool; if any sanity test fails or error-rate >0.5% on canary for 24h, auto-fallback to last pinned variant and create an incident ticket.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake UI enforces the required metadata fields and rejects submissions missing tokenizer_family or kv_layout_signature. 2) CI pipeline runs the three sanity suites and marks compatibility label. 3) Platform routes unpinned variants to a canary namespace and applies metrics guardrails. 4) Canary runbook executed and auto-rollback triggers on defined error thresholds. 5) Documentation page exists describing label semantics, example intake metadata, and operator troubleshooting checklist. 6) E2E test added to the catalog-evals suite that simulates a canary failure and verifies rollback occurs and a ticket is created.
metrics_success: Reduced manual triage by 40% for intake-related runtime issues within first quarter post-launch; <0.5% of canary swaps result in silent failures; canary rollback latency <5 minutes from threshold breach.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal only): gate enabled for internal models for 2 weeks; Phase 2 (beta): enable for partner submissions and Dedicated deployments at 10% traffic; Phase 3 (public): default enforcement for hosted catalog submissions with monitoring dashboards. Canary weights: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated metric checks between steps.
implementation_notes: Runtime team to expose a compatibility API endpoint that accepts the declared metadata and returns a runtime-routing decision plus normalized labels. Evals team to implement tokenization and KV continuity checks in catalog-evals harness. Console team to add intake form validation and label display. PM to author intake templates and examples. Keep compatibility label set extensible.
open_questions: 1) Do we allow a "soft-pin" override for Enterprise customers? 2) Should we require signed manifests for private deployments? 3) What is the acceptable similarity metric for deterministic snapshot tests? Recommend cosine >= 0.88 for classification prompts but need consensus. 4) Which infra owners sign off on auto-rollback policy for on-prem clusters?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly strict gates block useful models. Mitigation: soft-pin path and appeal flow. Risk: false positives from nondeterminism in quantized models. Mitigation: allow tolerance thresholds and require multiple run seeds. Risk: adversarial model submissions can exploit function-calling hooks. Mitigation: quarantine canary execution and strict network IAM for canary containers.
notes: This slate was drafted after two incidents where tokenization mismatches caused production drift during model promotion. The intake schema should be small and machine-parseable to enable fast routing decisions.
audit_trail: 2026-03-14: created by Ava Martinez; 2026-03-15: updated with implementation owners and revised similarity threshold recommendation by Liam Chen.
